scope: Deterministic work contracts plus a frozen local Debug Parquet control comparison. The candidate ran during native and E2E validation; this experiment does not establish a latency or throughput improvement.

conclusions.control: All 48 baseline/candidate samples match independent expected IDs and retain 21 decorations. Candidate warm medians are 25–27 ms versus 22–24 ms previously under different concurrent load; no latency improvement is claimed.
conclusions.routing: Nine authenticated real-segment routes yield two admitted identities, prune seven, and preserve full-corpus offsets 0 and 8. Comparator checks retain equal primary ties, reverse and backward pages, signed pre-epoch times, exact integers, and conservative malformed evidence fallback.
conclusions.lineage: Eight admitted pages reach eight concurrent I/O reads with eight lanes and one under saturation. All submitted reads join on failure; every returned byte remains owned. This is a scheduler contract, not a real-cloud latency benchmark.
conclusions.refresh: Both captured and projected real-Parquet paths gather one changed row and reuse 256 keys in a 257-row fragment. Deletion gathers zero and reuses all 256 remaining keys. A changed cohort or absent cache gathers all 256 remaining rows. Dependency traversal retains the cache while query coordinate views omit it.
conclusions.upgrade: The frozen old executable returns zero root matches and two alias matches for the exclusion fixture. Automatic repair on the final executable returns only beta for the root and alpha for the alias; alias-only leakage also repairs, and both results survive another restart.
